title: California's 49th Congressional District General Election, 2026
description: This is the general election for California's 49th Congressional District, covering coastal North San Diego County and southern Orange County. Incumbent Democrat Mike Levin, first elected in 2018 by flipping a historically Republican seat, faces Republican challenger Armen Kurdian, a retired Navy captain. The district was significantly reshaped by Proposition 50 in 2025, shifting its boundaries southward and making it more Democratic-leaning with a Cook Partisan Voter Index of D+4. Levin has won four consecutive competitive elections in this district by focusing on environmental policy, veterans' affairs, and nuclear waste removal from San Onofre, while Kurdian is emphasizing cost of living, education reform, and job creation as his top priorities.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for the CA-49 general election matchup. Cook Political Report rates the race as 'Likely Democratic' (as of November 2025).

candidates.name: Mike Levin
candidates.summary: Mike Levin is the incumbent U.S. Representative for California's 49th Congressional District, first elected in 2018. He is an attorney specializing in energy and environmental law, a graduate of Stanford University and Duke University School of Law, and serves on the House Appropriations Committee. Levin has focused on clean energy, spent nuclear fuel removal from San Onofre, veterans' benefits, and affordable healthcare, passing 35 bipartisan laws during his tenure.

candidates.name: Armen Kurdian
candidates.summary: Armen Kurdian is a Republican candidate and retired U.S. Navy captain running for California's 49th Congressional District. He served 25 years in the Navy as a Naval Flight Officer and engineering leader, earning a BS in Aerospace Engineering from the University of Kansas, an MS from the Naval Postgraduate School, and an MBA from Cornell/Queens University. Kurdian now works as a Lead Associate and Senior Systems Engineer at Booz Allen Hamilton and previously ran for Vista City Council in 2022, campaigning on lowering the cost of living, improving education, and creating jobs.

forecast.rationale: No public polling exists for CA-49, so the forecast relies entirely on non-polling fundamentals. Incumbent Democrat Mike Levin has won four consecutive competitive elections in this district since flipping it in 2018. The district was redrawn by Proposition 50 in 2025 to be more Democratic-leaning, now with a Cook Partisan Voter Index of D+4. Cook Political Report rates the race as 'Likely Democratic.' Levin holds key committee assignments (Appropriations) and has passed 35 bipartisan laws. Republican challenger Armen Kurdian is a credible candidate with a strong Navy background but has limited electoral experience (narrowly lost a Vista City Council race) and no campaign finance data available. The fundamentals point to a clear Democratic advantage, but the complete absence of public polling and sparse independent ratings keep confidence at medium rather than high.
